 On the show What We Know About the Alleged Killing On the MSC Seascape Cruise Ship
 A 48-year-old man has been arrested and charged with murder after his wife was found dead on a cruise ship off the coast of Galveston, Texas. Nov. 11, 2026, 11:04 AM EST / Source : TODAY Scott Stump
 Child Found in Cabin Where Man Allegedly Killed Wife on Cruise 01:59 Share Add TODAY to Google A Texas man is facing a federal murder charge after he told FBI investigators that he struck and choked his wife in their cabin aboard a cruise ship off the coast of Texas, according to a criminal complaint.
 The accused man, Jason Leon Watford, 48, was seen on video being escorted off the ship on Nov. 9 and arrested by law enforcement after a woman, later identified as his wife, was found dead on the MSC Seascape. A child was also involved in the situation, an FBI spokesperson told NBC News. 
 The cruise ship has since returned to sea with thousands of passengers shaken by the alleged killing. 
 Here’s what we know about what happened about the MSC Seascape.
 What Happened Aboard the Cruise Ship? 
 At approximately 7:46 p.m. local time on Nov. 8, Jason Leon Watford, 48, was seen on surveillance video entering a cabin on the MSC Seascape, followed by a woman about 25 minutes later, according to a criminal complaint filed by the FBI in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas. 
 At 9:02 p.m., a housekeeper arrived to deliver towels to the cabin and noticed blood on Jason Leon Watford’s hand and pants and a woman lying “motionless” and “face down on the floor,” according to the complaint.
 An FBI Houston spokesperson identified the woman as Susan Watford, Jason Leon Watford’s wife. 
 After reviewing the security footage, the FBI conducted an interview with Jason Leon Watford. Per the criminal complaint, he said he and his wife had been arguing at a restaurant and it escalated into a verbal dispute back in their room that caused him to “snap.”
 He told the FBI he struck his wife multiple times and began to choke and strangle her, according to the complaint. He said he wrapped his right arm around her neck from behind while she was lying down, and he applied pressure to her neck “for four to five minutes and released his hold only after becoming exhausted.”
 Jason Leon Watford said she lay motionless on the floor for approximately 10 minutes before the housekeeper knocked on the door, and he did not contact the ship security or medical personnel during that time. 
 A child who is “part of the family” was “involved in the situation and found uninjured by law enforcement,” an FBI spokesperson told NBC News. Authorities declined to reveal how the child is related to the suspect and victim. 
 A Texas Department of Family and Protective Services spokesperson told NBC News Nov. 10 the child involved is “safe and in foster care.”
 What Is Jason Leon Watford Charged With? 
 Watford has been charged with murder in connection with the investigation, according to the complaint. He faces up to life in prison if convicted. 
 He was in the Galveston County Jail on a federal hold on Nov. 9, according to jail records. He appeared in court for an initial hearing on Nov. 10 and is due back in court on Nov. 16 for a probable cause hearing. 
 Watford had a public defender assigned to him on Nov. 10, who declined to comment to NBC News. 
 Texas court records show Watford pleaded guilty to a 2024 domestic assault charge involving his wife for grabbing her wrist. The charge was dismissed after he completed probation. 
 Where Is the MSC Seascape Now? 
 The MSC Seascape left Galveston, Texas, Nov. 8 but returned to port in the early morning on Nov. 9 after the death of Susan Watford.
 After Jason Leon Watford was escorted off the cruise ship by law enforcement and arrested, the 1,060-foot vessel returned to sea that same day. 
 “The ship has since left the port and resumed its planned itinerary,” an MSC Cruises spokesperson said Nov. 9.
 The ship was scheduled to travel to Costa Maya, the Roatan Islands and Cozumel before returning to Texas on Nov. 15.
 Passenger Ally Edgar was at a show on the cruise ship with her family at the time of the alleged attack. She spoke with NBC’s Ryan Chandler in an interview that aired on TODAY Nov. 11. 
 “They made an announcement on the intercom, and so the theater show had stopped for a little bit,” she said. “We had looked up what the code had meant, and it said ‘life-threatening emergency.’” 
 Passengers are trying to come to grips with what allegedly happened now that the cruise has resumed. 
 “I feel like vibes are very low,” Edgar said. “It’s like, just an ominous feeling.” 
 Cruise operators MSC told NBC News the company is “cooperating fully with the investigation and providing support to those impacted.”
 A Maritime Attorney Weighs In on What’s Next 
 Maritime attorney Cara Miller told Chandler on TODAY that because the alleged killing happened in international waters, it could complicate the charges. 
 “The FBI has jurisdiction to investigate any and prosecute any type of crime that happens in international waters,” she said.
